title: Crash points anchored to message dispatch events
description: Add an opt-in explorer config field crash_after_send_probability (default 0.0). When a generated plan contains a Crash event for node N that is dependency-eligible, and the scheduler observes node N dispatch a remote message, with probability p immediately prioritize that Crash runnable (boost its selection score to ~1.0 for the next few steps). Implement in spur-core/src/simulator/core/scheduler.rs score path + a small state hook where dispatches are recorded; thread config through ExplorerConfig -> SingleRunConfig -> scheduler state. Enable at 0.3 in scheduler_configs/loop/general_vr.json.
rationale: The oracle bug (and many crash-recovery protocol bugs) requires a node to crash in the narrow window after sending a message and before its delivery. Random crash placement almost never lands there; H1 hazard rate is ~28% per run but the crash rarely hits the critical sender.
generalityArgument: Anchors crashes to a universal protocol event (any remote send by any node), no function names or protocol structure involved.

title: Hold in-flight messages of a crashed sender until it recovers
description: Add opt-in config field orphan_hold_probability (default 0.0). When a node crashes while messages it dispatched are still undelivered, with probability p per message move those messages into purgatory with release scheduled at/after the sender's Recover event (or a bounded delay if it never recovers). Implement alongside the existing purgatory in core/exec.rs + scheduler crash path (crash_node already walks queues). Enable at 0.5 in general_vr.json.
rationale: Directly manufactures the H2 stale-incarnation hazard: a message from a dead incarnation delivered after the node is back. H2 measured at ~19-26% incidentally; making it deliberate should sharply lift P(depth>=5..7) where the oracle chain needs pre-crash StartViewChange-class messages delivered post-recovery.
generalityArgument: Purely about crash/dispatch/delivery timing relationships; applies to every message type on every protocol.

title: Turn on message-delay purgatory in the general config
description: Set purgatory: {delay_probability: 0.15, delay_duration_range: [5, 100]} in scheduler_configs/loop/general_vr.json. No Rust changes.
rationale: Purgatory exists but is disabled by default and the loop config never enables it; delayed messages are a precondition for several oracle chain links (old messages arriving after recovery).
generalityArgument: Config-only, protocol-agnostic delay mechanism that already exists.

title: Turn on timeline feedback + steer in the general config
description: Set feedback: {mode: "timeline", steer: true} in scheduler_configs/loop/general_vr.json. No Rust changes. Measure ladder + utilization (steer divergent picks) vs baseline.
rationale: The feedback/steer machinery exists but the loop's general config runs feedback off; the utilization counters show whether steer actually changes decisions, and the ladder shows whether that helps.
generalityArgument: Existing generic novelty mechanism; no protocol knowledge.

title: Remove the dead randomly_drop_msgs code path
description: The schedule_runnable parameter randomly_drop_msgs is hardwired false at both call sites; the 30% drop branch is dead code. Remove the parameter and branch (flag-off stage is trivially satisfied since it is already off). Non-inferiority expected to be exact.
rationale: Dead code in the scheduler hot path is noise for every future hypothesis; removing it is free simplification and validates the ablation pipeline end to end.
generalityArgument: Removes nothing observable; pure code hygiene.

title: Incarnation-aware timeline novelty tuples
description: Track a per-node incarnation counter (increments on Recover) in run state. Extend TimelineTuple (feedback.rs) with a small incarnation-crossing flag: whether the delivered message was dispatched in an earlier incarnation of the sender or delivered to a node in a later incarnation than at dispatch time. Behind config field incarnation_novelty: bool (default false). With steer on, novel crossing tuples get chased automatically.
rationale: Post-recovery deliveries of pre-crash messages are exactly the transitions the oracle chain needs (links 4-7); making them first-class novelty targets lets existing steer machinery hunt them.
generalityArgument: Incarnation counting is protocol-independent (crash/recover are simulator events).

title: Fire timers on at most one node per window
description: Add queue-policy option timer_exclusive: bool (default false): when the timer queue is selected, prefer timers belonging to a single 'active timeout node' chosen per window (e.g. rotate every K steps), instead of any node's timer. Implement as a wrapper in core/queue_selector.rs. Enable in general_vr.json.
rationale: The oracle scenario needs exactly one backup to time out (starting a view change) while others stay quiet; when all backups race, view changes trample each other and the single-suspect pattern almost never occurs.
generalityArgument: One-suspect-at-a-time is a generic failure-detector pattern, not a VR concept.

title: PCT-style priority change points selector
description: Add within_queue_selector variant {type: "Pct", depth: d}: assign random static priorities to runnables and at d random steps during the run demote the currently-highest class (classic probabilistic concurrency testing). Implement in core/queue_selector.rs behind the existing selector enum; default remains Tournament. Try depth 3-8 in general_vr.json.
rationale: PCT gives provable lower bounds on hitting bugs of small depth; the oracle bug's depth may be within reach where uniform random is hopeless.
generalityArgument: PCT is a general-purpose concurrency testing algorithm.

title: Use hazard events as fitness for genetic/AOS modes
description: Count H1/H2-style hazard events in-run (sender-crash-with-inflight, post-recovery delivery of pre-crash message — the simulator knows dispatch/crash/recover/delivery ordering) into cheap per-run counters; add feedback mode "hazard" (or blend weight) so plan_score rewards runs that manufacture hazards. Behind config; default off. Then run genetic/AOS with hazard fitness in a variant general config.
rationale: Timeline novelty rewards any new ordering; hazard fitness rewards exactly the crash-recovery races the ladder measures, closing the loop between grading and searching without leaking the oracle.
generalityArgument: Hazard definitions reference only simulator-level events (dispatch, crash, recover, deliver).

title: Reduce explorer memory footprint (Arc/imbl clone traffic)
description: The explorer peaks at ~20G on 13.5k-run sessions (OOM-killed the daemon once) and the perf profile shows 26.5% of cycles in memmove from Arc::make_mut and imbl persistent-vector promote/push. Reduce allocation/clone traffic on the hot execution path: candidates include avoiding make_mut on shared values that are then dropped, small-value inlining, reusing per-run buffers in the parquet writer, or bounding retained per-run state. Behind config where semantics could shift; pure allocation changes need no flag. Verify with the A/B bench plus `/usr/bin/time -v` peak-RSS comparison.
rationale: Memory is now the binding constraint on evaluation size (20G peaks vs 30G box), and the same clone traffic dominates CPU; one fix likely buys both throughput and headroom.
generalityArgument: Pure implementation efficiency; no scheduling semantics involved.
